title: Introducing Trace Imports for Mastra Platform
summary: Import and inspect existing trace history.
body_markdown:
You can now import existing traces from third-party observability providers using[trace imports](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/observability#import-existing-traces) .


Imported traces show up alongside your Mastra-generated traces in Mastra platform (and deployed Studio), letting you debug, filter and compare across your trace history without switching between tools.


We're starting today with[Langfuse](https://mastra.ai/integrations/observability/langfuse) support, with more providers to follow.


Switching observability providers often means losing valuable trace history, with existing data left behind on the previous provider. By using trace imports, you can switch to Mastra and bring your trace history with you.


Your browser does not support the video tag.


Before trace imports, Mastra observability data could only be exported to third-party providers. Now you can pull it back with the details preserved: span types like` agent_run` ,` model_generation` and` tool_call` stay intact, along with parent-child structure, timestamps, inputs, outputs, usage and cost. Only trace observations are imported; scores, feedback, datasets, attachments and logs are omitted.


## Get started


Upgrade the Mastra CLI and` @mastra/core` dependencies:


Terminal


```text
npm   install   -g   mastra@latest
npm   install   @mastra/core@latest
```


note


Requires` mastra@1.34.1` and` @mastra/core@1.77.0` or later, added in[PR #24145](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/24145) and[PR #26779](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/26779) .


Trace imports target a Mastra project[deployed](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/deploy) to Mastra platform. The project's access token and ID should already be set in` .env` :


.env


```text
MASTRA_PLATFORM_ACCESS_TOKEN  =
MASTRA_PROJECT_ID  =
```


To import traces from a Langfuse project, create an[API key](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/public-api) under Settings → API Keys in Langfuse, then add the following environment variables to your` .env` :


.env


```text
LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY  =
LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY  =
LANGFUSE_BASE_URL  =  https://us.cloud.langfuse.com
```


` LANGFUSE_BASE_URL` defaults to the EU region. Set it to your[Langfuse region](https://langfuse.com/security/data-regions) , or self-hosted URL.


### Preview an import


Set` --target-project` to the name of your deployed Mastra project, and use` --dry-run` to preview an import:


Terminal


```text
mastra   traces   import   langfuse   --target-project   mastra-trace-imports   --dry-run
```


Output:


```text
┌  Mastra trace import
│
◇  Resolving Mastra Platform project
│
◇  Reading langfuse traces
│
◇  Prepared trace import ─────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                         │
│  Import ID:       25992b5f...                                           │
│  Source:          Langfuse project "langfuse-trace-imports"             │
│  (cmv54rv6...) at https://us.cloud.langfuse.com                         │
│  Target:          Mastra Platform project "mastra-trace-imports"        │
│  (53fc3cf2...)                                                          │
│  Window:          2026-09-14T08:57:54.479Z to 2026-10-14T08:57:54.479Z  │
│  Prepared:        6 traces / 146 spans                                  │
│  Skipped:         0 traces / 0 spans                                    │
│  Local data:      916.5 KiB                                             │
│                                                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
│
└  Dry run complete. Upload later with:
mastra traces import langfuse --resume 25992b5f... --target-project mastra-trace-imports
```


## Import


Omit` --dry-run` to import the traces. The CLI shows the same summary, asks for confirmation, uploads, then verifies. You can use` --yes` to skip the confirmation:


Terminal


```text
mastra   traces   import   langfuse   --target-project   mastra-trace-imports   --yes
```


```text
◇  Uploading prepared traces
│
◇  Verifying a sample through Mastra Platform
│
◆  Imported 6 traces / 146 spans.
│
└  Trace import complete. Report: ~/.mastra/imports/traces/53fc3cf2.../25992b5f.../report.json
```


## Date window


To import traces from a specific date range, use the` --since` and` --until` flags with ISO 8601 timestamps:


Terminal


```text
mastra   traces   import   langfuse   --target-project   ...   --since   2026-10-01T00:00:00Z   --until   2026-10-12T00:00:00Z
```


## Resume


To continue an import that was interrupted, or to upload one you previewed with` --dry-run` , use the` --resume` flag with the import ID:


Terminal


```text
mastra   traces   import   langfuse   --target-project   ...   --resume   25992b5f...
```


For more information and full configuration options, see:


- [Import existing traces](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/observability#import-existing-traces)
- [mastra traces import reference](https://mastra.ai/reference/cli/mastra#mastra-traces-import)
- [Observability on Mastra platform](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/observability)
- [LangfuseExporter reference](https://mastra.ai/reference/observability/tracing/exporters/langfuse)
- [Langfuse integration](https://mastra.ai/integrations/observability/langfuse)
- [Langfuse API keys](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/public-api)
- [Langfuse data regions](https://langfuse.com/security/data-regions)
